evals.name: first-run-html-article
evals.prompt: I'm getting into Swift concurrency and want to start keeping a vocab list. Scan this article I saved and build the list from it: fixtures/swift-concurrency-article.html
evals.user_answers: Scope: subject Swift, level intermediate, include concepts + keywords/attributes + multi-word phrases, exclude names from the article author's own app and product names; known terms: async, await. Approve every candidate you recommend. Accept the drafts as written.
evals.expected_output: A new Swift list with that scope; 6+ entries each with definition, example, use_case; no async/await; no app-specific identifiers; definitions free of the app name; a Markdown view.

evals.name: session-scan-two-lists
evals.prompt: Go through my session from last week (the transcript is at fixtures/past-session-v2.jsonl) and add anything worth learning to my vocab lists.
evals.user_answers: Add every new term you recommend. For any possible duplicate of an existing entry, keep the existing entry and fold the new form in as an alias rather than adding a second entry. Accept drafts as written.
evals.expected_output: AI terms routed to the AI list, no second MainActor entry, RAG folded into retrieval-augmented generation as an alias, new entries complete with provenance and dated 2026-09-20, the session's own date, not today's. Also: 'token' is a known term in the AI list's scope and must not be added; 'reference cycle' from the session is folded into the existing 'retain cycle' as an alias.

evals.name: export-to-tutorial-creator
evals.prompt: Send my Swift vocab terms over to tutorial-creator so I can review them with flashcards. My tutorial vocabulary file is fixtures/tc/vocabulary.yaml.
evals.user_answers: Yes, go ahead after showing me what will change.
evals.expected_output: Three new terms appended to the tutorial-creator file without altering existing bytes; @MainActor skipped as already present; appended entries start at status new; undo marker written; user told to run regen-md, which brings VOCABULARY.md in step with the yaml in place. Exported entries use first_encountered.context 'external source', which regen-md files under an 'External source' section.

evals.name: tc-roundtrip-regen-undo
evals.prompt: Send my Swift vocab terms to tutorial-creator and refresh its VOCABULARY.md so they show up. My tutorial project is fixtures/tcproj.
evals.user_answers: Yes, go ahead after showing me what will change. If regen-md asks about terms that exist only in VOCABULARY.md, keep them. Follow-up after the refresh: 'Actually, undo that export. I want to redo it later.'
evals.expected_output: The refresh adds the three exported terms to VOCABULARY.md under an External source section (plus rows for the fixture's other yaml-only terms) and leaves every prior row, heading and Source line in place; regen-md asks about the terms that exist only in the view instead of erasing them, and they are kept. tutorial-creator's vocab undo then restores the exact original term set, consumes the marker, and removes the three rows and the External source section they created.

evals.name: import-from-tutorial-creator
evals.prompt: Start a Testing vocab list and pull in the testing-related terms I already have in tutorial-creator.
evals.user_answers: Scope: subject Software testing, level intermediate, include concepts, techniques, and multi-word phrases; exclude tool and product names; no known terms. Import every testing term you find. Accept the drafts as written, including any examples you write.
evals.expected_output: A new Testing list with 8+ imported terms, all complete, examples split out of use_case, no learning state copied, tutorial-creator provenance recorded, tutorial-creator file untouched, Swift list untouched.
